(Los Angeles, California) | college = [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] (2018–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2022 | years1 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]] | team1 = [[Motor City Cruise]] | years2 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023-24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = [[Capital City Go-Go]] | years3 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team3 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years4 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team4 = →Capital City Go-Go | years5 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team5 = [[Cleveland Charge]] | years6 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team6 = [[Iowa Wolves]] | highlights = }} '''Jules Liam Bernard''' (born January 21, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. ==High school career== Bernard played basketball for [[Windward School]] in [[Los Angeles]].{{cite web |last1=Bolch |first1=Ben |title=With 'no quit in him,' UCLA's Jules Bernard thrives off relentlessness |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-01-21/ucla-basketball-jules-bernard |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=November 22, 2021 |date=January 21, 2021}} As a junior, he averaged 25.3 points and 13.7 rebounds per game. In his senior season, Bernard averaged 26.4 points and 14.2 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Flores |first1=Ronnie |title=Boys BB: All-State Best of Best 2018 |url=https://www.calhisports.com/2018/04/26/boys-bb-all-state-best-of-best-2018/ |website=Cal-Hi Sports |access-date=November 22, 2021 |date=April 26, 2018}} He competed for the Compton Magic on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last1=Bossi |first1=Eric |title=Top 50 wing Jules Bernard sets three visits |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/top-50-wing-jules-bernard-sets-three-visits |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=November 22, 2021 |date=September 14, 2017}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] in October 2017 over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=ESPN 100 forward Jules Bernard verbally commits to UCLA Bruins |url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/20982305/jules-bernard-verbally-commits-ucla-bruins |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 22, 2021 |date=October 10, 2017}} He was attracted to the Bruins by their program's history and head coach [[Steve Alford]] being open to playing skilled freshmen.{{cite news|first=Cam|last=Smith|title=UCLA basketball lands signature 2018 commitment from 4-star SG Jules Bernard|date=October 11, 2017|newspaper=USA Today|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/ucla-basketball-lands-signature-2018-commitment-from-4-star-sg-jules-bernard|access-date=January 29, 2022}} ==College career== As a freshman at UCLA, Bernard averaged 7.6 points and 3.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Bossi |first1=Eric |title=Bossi's Best: Players who should make big leaps as sophomores |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/bossi-s-best-players-who-should-make-big-leaps-as-sophomores |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=November 22, 2021 |date=September 11, 2019}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 5.5 points and 2.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Jules Bernard – Men's Basketball |url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jules-bernard/10521 |website=UCLA Athletics |access-date=November 22, 2021}} On March 3, 2021, he scored a career-high 23 points in an 82–72 loss to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Suffers 82-74 Setback at Oregon |url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2021/3/3/mens-basketball-suffers-82-74-setback-at-oregon.aspx |website=UCLA Athletics |access-date=November 22, 2021 |date=March 3, 2021}} As a junior, Bernard averaged 10.3 points and 5.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Rothstein |first1=Jon |title=The Breakfast Buffet: Andre Curbelo leads Illinois against Marquette, Florida, Jules Bernard |url=https://collegehoopstoday.com/index.php/rothstein-files/the-breakfast-buffet-andre-curbelo-leads-illinois-against-marquette-florida-jules-bernard/ |website=College Hoops Today |date=November 15, 2021 |access-date=November 22, 2021}} In his senior year in [[2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2021–22]], he continued to decrease his [[turnover (basketball)|turnovers]] after nearly committing twice as many turnovers as [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s in his first two seasons.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Remarkable ascent of UCLA senior Jules Bernard elicits praise from his coach|date=January 7, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-01-07/ascent-of-ucla-senior-jules-bernard-elicis-praise-mick-cronin|access-date=January 9, 2022}} He had a season-high 22 points in each of the Bruins' two games against [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]].{{cite news|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=Improved Jules Bernard leads UCLA back into Pac-12 play|date=January 7, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/01/07/improved-jules-bernard-leads-ucla-back-into-pac-12-play/|access-date=January 9, 2022}}{{cite news|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA basketball returns, routs Long Beach State|date=January 6, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/01/06/ucla-basketball-returns-routs-long-beach-state/|access-date=January 9, 2022}} Bernard ended the season with nine consecutive games scoring in double figures, including a team-high 16 points in UCLA's season-ending loss to [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in the Sweet Sixteen of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA's March Madness run ends in heartbreaking Sweet 16 loss to North Carolina|date=March 25, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-25/ucla-mens-basketball-north-carolina-march-madness|access-date=March 26, 2022}}{{cite magazine|first=Jeremy|last=Woo|title=Players Who Need to Step Up in the Sweet 16|date=March 24, 2022|magazine=Sports Illustrated|url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/03/24/morning-madness-ncaa-tournament-x-factor-players-sweet-16|access-date=March 26, 2022}} As a senior, Bernard averaged 12.8 points and 4.7 rebounds per game. After the season, he [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] for the [[NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent to maintain his college eligibility; the NCAA allowed an extra year due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news|title=UCLA's Jules Bernard to enter NBA draft, won't hire agent|date=April 20, 2022|publisher=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-business-sports-college-basketball-mens-2597bab74a73617c27a0be484b36f474|access-date=April 26, 2022}} He was invited to the [[NBA G League Elite Camp]] but did not receive an invitation to the [[NBA Draft Combine]]. He had a workout with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] before deciding to remain in the draft, minutes before the deadline to return to school.{{cite news|first=Kyle|last=Goon|title=UCLA's Jules Bernard remains in NBA draft after Lakers workout|date=June 1, 2022|work=The Orange County Register|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/06/01/uclas-jules-bernard-remains-in-nba-draft-after-lakers-workout/|access-date=June 2, 2022}}{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jules Bernard announces he has played final game with UCLA|date=June 1, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-06-01/jules-bernard-announces-hes-played-final-game-with-ucla|access-date=June 2, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Motor City Cruise (2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Bernard played with the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|first=Keith|last=Langlois|title=Ivey & Duren get Pistons off and running in Summer League win over Blazers|date=July 8, 2022|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/ivey-duren-get-pistons-off-and-running|access-date=July 14, 2022}} He scored in double digits once in the first four games before scoring a team-high 22 points in the finale, including 14 points in the third quarter.{{cite news|first=Omari II|last=Sankofa|title=Jules Bernard, Charlie Moore shine as Detroit Pistons close Summer League with 102-86 win|date=July 16, 2022|work=Detroit Free Press|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/07/16/bernard-moore-spearhead-pistons-102-86-summer-league-win/10078887002/|access-date=July 20, 2022}} He was later added to the Pistons' training camp roster after signing an [[Exhibit 10]] contract.{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Curtis|title=Pistons' Kemba Walker not with team; three have injuries heading into training camp|date=September 26, 2022|work=The Detroit News|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/09/26/pistons-announce-training-camp-roster-injury-updates-kemba-walker-not-with-team/69519196007/|access-date=September 29, 2022}} Bernard played in three of the team's four preseason games before being released.{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Curtis|title=Report: Pistons expected to waive Kemba Walker|date=October 14, 2022|work=The Detroit News|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/10/14/pistons-expected-to-waive-kemba-walker/69563043007/|access-date=October 18, 2022}} He was later named to the training camp roster for the [[Motor City Cruise]], the Pistons' [[G League]] affiliate.{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Curtis|title=Veteran guard Alec Burks should add to Pistons' second unit once healthy|date=October 25, 2022|work=The Detroit News|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/10/25/guard-alec-burks-should-add-to-detroit-pistons-2nd-unit-once-healthy/69588814007/|access-date=October 26, 2022}} ===Capital City Go-Go (2022–2023)=== On December 22, 2022, Bernard was traded from the Motor City to the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 22, 2022}} On October 1, 2023, Bernard signed with the [[Washington Wizards]],{{cite tweet|author=Washington Wizards|title=Official: We have signed Jules Bernard to an Exhibit 10 contract. We have also placed Dejan Vasiljevic on waivers.|number=1708577479110062200|user=WashWizards|date=October 1, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite tweet|author=Washington Wizards|title=Official: We have signed Devon Dotson to an Exhibit 10 contract. We have also waived Jules Bernard.|number=1715061519132537083|user=WashWizards|date=October 19, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2023}} On October 30, he returned to Capital City.{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster, Dates|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster-dates|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 26, 2023}} ===Washington Wizards (2023–2024)=== On December 8, 2023, Bernard signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Jules Bernard to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-jules-bernard-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}} On the same day, Bernard made his NBA debut for the Wizards in a 124–97 loss to the [[2023–24 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]]. ===Cleveland Charge (2024–2025)=== On September 24, 2024, Bernard signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]],{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Cavs Adding Four Players To Fortify Camp Roster|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/cavs-adding-four-players-to-fortify-camp-roster.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-roster-update-241019|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On October 26, he joined the [[Cleveland Charge]].{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2024-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}} ===Iowa Wolves (2025–present)=== On November 6, 2025, Bernard was named to the [[Iowa Wolves]]' opening night roster.{{cite web|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/iowa-wolves-announce-opening-night-roster|title=Iowa Wolves Announce Opening Night Roster|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 6, 2025|access-date=November 6, 2025}} On February 25, 2026, Bernard signed a two-way contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web|title=Jules Bernard gets two-way contract from Timberwolves|url=https://www.startribune.com/jules-bernard-gets-two-way-contract-from-timberwolves/601588740|access-date=March 8, 2026|website=startribune.com|language=en}} However, three days later he was waived by Minnesota without having appeared for the team.{{Cite web|title=Timberwolves Waive Jules Bernard|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-jules-bernard|access-date=March 8, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
